paragraphs.source_en: The main room of the mountain retreat teahouse was three tatami mats in size. Sen no Sōeki came as far as the citrus gate and respectfully ushered the guests into the tearoom. Today’s Hideyoshi was utterly unlike the man he was in camp. Seated in the room with tea masters Tsuda Sōgyū, Naya Shōan, Mandaiya Sōan, Sumiyoshiya Sōmu, and others, he was exceptionally humble in manner.

paragraphs.source_en: First Hideyoshi would show them this peerless castle and fully impress them with his majesty; then he would bring them to this exquisitely elegant teahouse. By the time Hideyoshi had solemnly served the tea, most of the warriors must already have been thoroughly bewildered. Nor should one forget the other golden tearoom, where he would flaunt a tea kettle made of gold. In truth, this inward ostentation and outward humility were essentially one and the same: devices for overawing everyone present.
